newsitem.title: INDIA: India sugar rallies, talk of extra quota fades.
newsitem.headline: India sugar rallies, talk of extra quota fades.

text.p: Sugar prices bounced back after a recent setback on the local market, dealers said.
Fresh consumer buying lifted prices upward while limited arrivals kept offerings at a low ebb.
"Earlier in the week market reacted on fear that government may release more free sale quota but today prices bounced back as no such announcement came through," one broker said.
In the ready delivery sugar S-30 rose by 5 rupees at 1,375/1,430 rupees per quintal while sugar M-30 rose by 15 rupees at 1,435/1,505 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery climbed up to 1,335/1,355 rupees per quintal from 1,325/1,335 rupees on higher outstation buying as well as increased lifting by the bulk consumers at mill level.
Free sale quota for current month is 750,000 tonnes while it was 700,000 tonnes last month.
